auth.description: GitHub token sent as a bearer — a GitHub App installation token, a fine-grained PAT, or a classic PAT
auth.name: github.token
auth.subject: unstated

auth.description: GitHub OAuth2 access token obtained on behalf of a signed-in user. Bounded by that user's own permissions, never by the application's
auth.name: github.oauth_token
auth.subject: user

config.help: Register an OAuth app under Settings -> Developer settings -> OAuth Apps, with the callback URL your deployment serves. This is the client ID, which is public
config.label: GitHub OAuth application client ID
config.name: oauth_client_id

config.help: The callback address this deployment serves, registered on the app above. GitHub matches the host (excluding sub-domains) and port exactly and requires the path to be at or below the registered callback URL's path — so a registered `https://host/api/oauth` admits `https://host/api/oauth/callback` but not `https://host/`
config.label: GitHub OAuth callback URL
config.name: oauth_redirect_uri

config.help: The client secret issued beside the ID above. GitHub shows it once at generation and never again. Supplied by whoever runs this deployment, never by an end user
config.label: GitHub OAuth application client secret
config.name: oauth_client_secret

description: GitHub REST API: discover the authenticated user, their organisations and reachable repositories; read repositories, commits, issues, pull requests and Actions workflow runs; and write issues and issue comments

operations.description: Get one repository's metadata, including its default branch, visibility and permissions

params.description: The repository owner — a user or organisation login
params.name: owner

params.description: The repository name, without the owner prefix
params.name: repo

archived.description: An archived repository is read-only — a write against it fails, so check this before `github-issue-create`

description.description: Null when the repository has none

full_name.description: `owner/repo`, which is how every other operation here addresses it

id.description: The repository's global id, stable across renames

open_issues_count.description: Open issues **and** open pull requests, since GitHub counts a PR as an issue

owner.description: The owning user or organisation: `login`, `id`, `type` (`User` or `Organization`), `avatar_url`, `html_url`

permissions.description: What the authenticated token can do here: `admin`, `push` and `pull` are always present, `maintain` and `triage` only sometimes. Absent entirely for an unauthenticated read

visibility.description: `public` or `private` per the reference; an enterprise repository can also be `internal`, so this is deliberately not a closed enum

operations.description: Get one issue by number. GitHub treats a pull request as an issue, so a PR number returns that PR's issue view; use github-pull-get for its merge and review state

params.description: The repository owner — a user or organisation login
params.name: owner

params.description: The repository name, without the owner prefix
params.name: repo

params.description: The issue number within the repository — the number in its URL, not its global id
params.name: issue_number

assignees.description: Everyone assigned. The reference's issue schema documents this array and does **not** document a singular `assignee`, so none is declared here even though the API returns one

body.description: The issue body as Markdown; null when the author wrote none

comments.description: How many comments it has — a count, not the comments

id.description: The issue's global id. For a pull request read through this endpoint it is an **issue** id and does not address the PR resource

labels.description: The applied labels, each `{id, name, color, description}`

number.description: The per-repository number — what this operation's `issue_number` takes

pull_request.description: PRESENT ONLY IF THIS IS A PULL REQUEST — `{url, html_url, diff_url, patch_url, merged_at}`. Its presence is how GitHub says the answer is a PR; read its merge and review state with `github-pull-get`, and note that `merged_at` here is null for an open or closed-unmerged PR

state_reason.description: Why it closed: `completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate` or `reopened`. Null on an open issue, and the difference between a fixed issue and a dismissed one

operations.description: Get one pull request by number, with its merge state, head and base refs and review counts

params.description: The repository owner — a user or organisation login
params.name: owner

params.description: The repository name, without the owner prefix
params.name: repo

params.description: The pull request number within the repository
params.name: pull_number

base.description: Where it would land: `{ref, sha, label, repo}`

body.description: The description as Markdown, or null

head.description: The source of the change: `{ref, sha, label, repo}` — `repo` is a different repository for a fork PR

id.description: The pull request's own id — distinct from the issue id `github-issue-get` returns for the same number

merge_commit_sha.description: The resulting commit once merged. Its nullability before a merge is not documented, so nothing is asserted here

mergeable.description: THREE-VALUED: true, false, or **null meaning not yet computed** — GitHub starts a background job on first read and the reference says to resubmit the request. Treat null as unknown, never as false

mergeable_state.description: GitHub's word for the merge situation, e.g. `clean`, `dirty`, `blocked`, `behind`, `unknown`

merged.description: Whether it landed. This is the settled answer; `mergeable` below is about whether it *could*

review_comments.description: Line-level review comments. Conversation comments are counted separately and are what `github-issue-comment-add` writes

state.description: `open` or `closed`. A merged PR is `closed`, so this cannot distinguish merged from abandoned — read `merged`

operations.description: Open a new issue on a repository. The issue is immediately visible to everyone who can see the repository and notifies its subscribers

params.description: The repository owner — a user or organisation login
params.name: owner

params.description: The repository name, without the owner prefix
params.name: repo

params.description: The issue title; the only required field
params.name: title

params.description: The issue body as GitHub-flavoured Markdown
params.name: body

params.description: Label names to apply; a name the repository does not have yet is created
params.name: labels

params.description: User logins to assign; GitHub silently drops any login without push access to the repository
params.name: assignees

assignees.description: Who was actually assigned. GitHub silently drops a login without push access, so compare this against what was requested rather than assuming it took

html_url.description: The issue's page — the link to give a human

labels.description: The labels that were applied. A name the repository did not have is created by this call and appears here

number.description: The per-repository number to address it by afterwards

user.description: The account the token belongs to — a created issue is attributed to it, not to whoever asked for it

operations.description: Add a comment to an issue or pull request. The comment is public to everyone who can see the repository and notifies its participants; GitHub has no private or internal comment here

params.description: The repository owner — a user or organisation login
params.name: owner

params.description: The repository name, without the owner prefix
params.name: repo

params.description: The issue or pull request number to comment on
params.name: issue_number

params.description: The comment text as GitHub-flavoured Markdown; must not be blank
params.name: body

author_association.description: The commenter's standing in the repository: `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`, `CONTRIBUTOR`, `NONE` and so on

html_url.description: Link to this comment, anchored — not to the issue

id.description: The comment's own id — not the issue's

issue_url.description: API URL of the issue or pull request that was commented on

reactions.description: Reaction rollup counts, all zero on a new comment

user.description: The commenting account, which is whoever the token belongs to

The default value for a merge commit message.

- `PR_TITLE` - default to the pull request's title.
- `PR_BODY` - default to the pull request's body.
- `BLANK` - default to a blank commit message.

merge_commit_title.description:
The default value for a merge commit title.

- `PR_TITLE` - default to the pull request's title.
- `MERGE_MESSAGE` - default to the classic title for a merge message (e.g., Merge pull request #123 from branch-name).

squash_merge_commit_message.description:
The default value for a squash merge commit message:

- `COMMIT_MESSAGES` - default to the branch's commit messages.
- `BLANK` - default to a blank commit message.

squash_merge_commit_title.description:
The default value for a squash merge commit title:

- `PR_TITLE` - default to the pull request's title.
- `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE` - default to the commit's title (if only one commit) or the pull request's title (when more than one commit).
